issues.description: Method parameter mismatch for Stock.findStockIngredient: The problem statement UML specifies a single-parameter method Stock.findStockIngredient(String) that returns StockIngredient. The solution implementation defines public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) (single parameter). The template, however, declares public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name, boolean caseSensitive) (two parameters) and therefore does not match the UML or solution. Additionally, the template's other Stock methods (add and take) invoke findStockIngredient(ingredient) with a single String argument, which will cause compilation errors. This inconsistency prevents students from compiling or running the template and confuses which API they must implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Stock.findStockIngredient declaration to match the UML and the solution: declare public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name). Update the implementation to perform the intended lookup (for example, use x.getName().equals(name) as in the solution) and remove the boolean parameter. Ensure internal calls (add, take, and any other usages) call the single-argument method. This will align the template with the problem statement and solution and prevent compilation errors.

issues.description: Concept: a method to find a StockIngredient by name. Problem statement / UML and the solution repository use a single-parameter method named findStockIngredient(String) returning StockIngredient. The template repository instead provides findStockIngredient(String, boolean) (an extra boolean caseSensitive parameter). Students reading the UML/description will expect findStockIngredient(String) but the starter code exposes a different signature, causing confusion about which method to call and how to implement interactions with Stock (e.g., acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice in the problem/solution use the single-argument form).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the problem statement and solution by providing the single-parameter method in the starter code. Add a public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) to src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java (either implement it or overload the existing method to delegate to findStockIngredient(name, <appropriate boolean>)). Alternatively, update the problem statement to document the two-parameter signature if the boolean parameter is intentional.
